name: store-en
title: English Chrome Web Store screenshot series
style: v5 — off-white ground (#F7F7F5) with a lime bloom top-right and a purple whisper bottom-left; lime is an accent, never the subject (commit dba00f2).
sourceOfTruth: slide1..4.html — English copy is inline in the HTML

captures.recapture: node apps/youtube/screenshots/capture-backdrop.mjs --locale en --learn es --native en --modes sidebar,guess,settings --theme-pref light
captures.note: Shared by every pipeline (~345 MB, 2560x1600 PNG) and therefore referenced, not vendored. render.mjs verifies these exist before launching a browser. Captured in the extension's OWN light theme (--class vtt-light puts the shipped vtt-light class on <html>) — NOT the legacy screenshots/light-theme.capture.css override, which predates the product having a light theme. Capture from a PROD build (plain `vite build`, no EXT_ENV=dev): a dev build paints a lime 'backend: env' switch across the top of the panel.

files: promo-1..4.png (1280x800, upload to CWS) + @2x (2560x1600, for the website)

knownIssues: slide1 does NOT use a product capture: it is the fullscreen@1 slide, vendored here (assets/fullscreen-*). Its panel is a REBUILT replica, measured off the running extension rather than captured, so it drifts silently if the product's panel changes. The other three slides embed real captures and would fail loudly on a missing one.
history: 2026-08-27: the fullscreen hero took slide 1, and the two slides it made redundant were dropped — the old opener ("Dual subtitles turn any video into a language lesson") and the old fullscreen slide ("Works on any video with subtitles"), whose claim the hero now carries. Both renders are kept under archive/2026-08-27-displaced-by-fullscreen-hero/. The series went 5 → 6 → 4; four is under the store's five-per-locale cap, so nothing has to be chosen at upload time.
